correctness.rationale: The polynomial generator identities are correct. Writing \(s=|X|^2\), \(R=\operatorname{Re}(\overline XY)\), and \(I=\operatorname{Im}(\overline XY)\), stationarity of \(Ls=2a(R-s)\) gives \(\int R=S\), while stationarity of \(LI=(c_1-a)I+c_2(s+R)\) gives \((c_1-a)\int I+2c_2S=0\). The displayed observable \(G=aR-(a+c_1)s/2\) satisfies \(LG=|\dot X|^2-ac_2I+a(2c_1-a-Z)s\). Eliminating \(\int I\) gives the claimed exact weighted-height identity. The auxiliary coboundary \(L(s-2aZ)=-2as+2abZ\) gives the mean law. On \(c_1=a\), \(c_2\ne0\), the \(I\)-balance forces \(S=0\), invariance then forces \(X=Y=0\), and the remaining scalar contraction forces the origin atom. The symbolic package verifier checks every polynomial identity exactly.

value.rationale: The theorem converts known trajectory algebra into a new exact statistical constraint for every compact recurrent state and identifies a sharp parameter plane where all compact recurrence collapses to the origin. It also explains the height of a published rotating orbit as one instance of a measure-wide law. That is a motivated structural recurrence result, not a routine restatement of an ultimate-bound estimate.
